strategy.title: No plan fits 2 owner hours a week
strategy.why: The only opening (heritage-tree condition surveys, ten written acceptances at $700) is fulfilled by the owner personally at 8 hours per survey. Reaching $5,000 needs 8 surveys = 64 owner hours; the goal allows about 9 owner hours over 30 days (2 h/week), enough for one survey ($700).

alternatives.title: Deliver one survey inside the hours allowed
alternatives.why: Fits the 9-hour budget but brings only $700 of the $5,000 target.

alternatives.title: Subcontract the surveys to an arborist
alternatives.why: No fulfiller other than the owner is recorded on the card, and no price or availability for one is evidenced.

steps.label: Find a qualified arborist/surveyor who can fulfil the signed surveys below $700 each, or openings Brain itself can fulfil, so owner time stays at or under 2 h/week

sources.claim: 8 hours of work per survey, fulfilled by the owner personally

noPlan.decisiveGap: Fulfilment is the owner personally at 8 hours per survey; the $5,000 target needs 8 surveys (64 hours) but the goal allows about 9 owner hours in the window, so the owner can fulfil only one ($700).
noPlan.resolution: Owner raises the time allowance to about 15-16 hours a week (64 hours over the window), or Brain finds a third-party fulfiller for the surveys at a cost below $700 each, or openings Brain can fulfil itself.

excluded.why: Needs 64 owner hours to reach the target against a 9-hour ceiling.

constraints.suggestion: Allow about 64 owner hours over the 30 days (~15 h/week), or permit a paid subcontractor to do the surveys.

disagreements.reason: Brain marks fulfilment ok because the owner fulfils personally (and only a person says so), but the owner can supply at most ~9 hours in the window against 64 needed, so fulfilment of the deals that reach the target is not available within the goal's limits.

review.reasons: NO_PLAN with an OWNER_HOURS constraint is correct. The owner is the recorded fulfiller at 8 h per $700 survey. The target needs 8 surveys ($5,600; 7 give only $4,900), which is 64 owner hours against about 9 hours allowed (2 h/week over 30 days), so only one survey fits. Brain's own verdict agrees (the agreed deals need more owner hours than the goal has). The author does not invent a subcontractor, because none is recorded with a price. The disagreement with Brain's FULFILMENT link is reasoned correctly.
findings: Minor: the suggested allowance of about 15-16 h/week understates what is needed. Deliveries must finish about 7 days before the deadline to settle, so 64 hours have to fit in roughly 23 days, about 19-20 h/week. This does not change the stance.
